title: Lovlina Borgohain Wins Gold on Her Birthday as India Powers Through Day 14
excerpt: On her 29th birthday, Lovlina Borgohain beat China's Bao Ziyi 5-0 to win 75kg boxing gold at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games — while India's women's recurve team stunned South Korea for a historic first gold and Sujeet Kalkal reached the 65kg wrestling final.
body:
• Lovlina Borgohain won the women's 75kg boxing gold on her 29th birthday, defeating China's Bao Ziyi 5-0 at Nishio — only the second Indian woman after Mary Kom to win Asian Games boxing gold.
  • India's women's recurve team — Ankita Bhakat, Kirti Sharma and 17-year-old Kumkum Mohod — stunned 10-time champions South Korea 5-3 to win India's first-ever Asian Games gold in the event.
  • World No. 1 Sujeet Kalkal beat Japan's Olympic champion Kotaro Kiyooka to reach the men's freestyle 65kg wrestling final.
  • Dhiraj Bommadevara and Kumkum Mohod added a mixed-team recurve silver, with India's tally at 11 golds and 68 medals overall.

Lovlina Borgohain picked the perfect day to deliver the perfect gift. On her 29th birthday, the Tokyo Olympic bronze medallist dismantled China's Bao Ziyi by a unanimous 5-0 decision to claim the women's 75kg boxing gold at the Asian Games in Nishio, Japan, on Friday. The win makes her only the second Indian woman boxer, after Mary Kom, to stand atop an Asian Games podium.

The final followed a pattern of growing dominance. Borgohain edged the opening round 3-2 before taking the next two rounds 4-1, with four judges scoring the bout 29-28 and one card reading 30-27 in her favour. Her route to gold included a 5-0 shutout of South Korea's Seong Suyeon in the quarterfinal and a hard-fought 3-2 split decision over Kazakhstan's Natalya Bogdanova in the semifinal — revenge of a sort after the same semifinalist had pushed her to the limit. It completes a career turnaround from the Hangzhou 2022 silver in the same weight class.

Context & Background

Borgohain's gold adds to a career that already includes an Olympic bronze, a World Championship gold in 2023 and a Commonwealth Games silver earlier this year. Her win also guaranteed India its best-ever Asian Games boxing haul may still grow — Ankush and Parveen Hooda have also reached finals, according to multiple reports.

The bigger shock came at the archery range. The women's recurve trio of Ankita Bhakat, Kirti Sharma and 17-year-old Kumkum Mohod stunned South Korea — ten-time Olympic champions — 5-3 in the final to win India's first-ever Asian Games gold in the event. India's first appearance in an Asian Games recurve team final ended with a famous win, secured when Kumkum landed a perfect 10 with the final arrow of the match. India had earlier beaten China 5-1 in the semifinal.

The archery story is one of steady building. This same core ended a five-year wait for a World Cup gold in Shanghai in May, beating Korea in the semifinal, and upgraded the bronze medals India won in 2010 and 2022. Kirti replaced former world number one Deepika Kumari, who failed to make the squad through the selection trials.

Impact & Analysis

Day 14 pushed India's tally to 11 golds and 68 medals overall (24 silver, 33 bronze), with the country seventh in the medal table at the time of writing. The archery gold is the one with the longest tail: beating Korea in a team final is the benchmark result Indian recurve archery has chased for a decade, and a 17-year-old delivered the decisive arrow.

The mixed-team recurve final added silver for Dhiraj Bommadevara and Kumkum Mohod, who fought back from 3-1 down to beat Japan 5-3 in the semifinal before losing 5-3 to China in the final. That final carried extra sting: the winning National Olympic Committee earns a men's and women's quota for the LA 2028 Olympics, and China's victory took those places.

"I am not fully satisfied with his performance. We showed only about 20 to 25 per cent of what we have worked on."

— Shako Bentinidis, coach of Sujeet Kalkal

On the wrestling mat, Sujeet Kalkal held his nerve against Japan's Olympic champion Kotaro Kiyooka to reach the men's freestyle 65kg final. His coach Shako Bentinidis was characteristically unsatisfied — "We have done only 20 per cent of the work. The remaining 80 per cent is for the final" — but beating an Olympic champion on home soil is a statement regardless. The gold-medal bout is scheduled for 2:46 PM IST.

Diaspora Angle

With boxing and archery finals drawing strong viewership from Indian households in the US, UK and the Gulf, Lovlina's birthday gold and the teenage heroics of Kumkum Mohod will resonate well beyond the Games — moments like these consistently drive the strongest engagement with diaspora audiences.

What's Next

Sujeet's 65kg final takes place this afternoon, with India chasing wrestling gold. Ankush and Parveen Hooda will also contest their boxing finals, meaning Day 15 could yet lift the boxing contingent past anything India has achieved at an Asian Games.
